patches.per_device_adaptation:
CRITICAL multi-GPU transform (SPEC risk #1). Upstream's streaming state is SINGLE-DEVICE. Our PP/TP runs up to 7 GPUs and `routed_moe_launch` derives the device via `int compact_dev=0; cudaGetDevice(&compact_dev); if(compact_dev<0||compact_dev>=DS4_CUDA_MAX_DEVICES) compact_dev=0;` (FORK 12627-12629). Mirror g_moe_compact_*[DS4_CUDA_MAX_DEVICES] (FORK 630-635) exactly.

CONVERT TO PER-DEVICE ARRAYS (index by compact_dev = current cudaGetDevice):
1. `static cuda_stream_selected_cache g_stream_selected_cache;` -> `[DS4_CUDA_MAX_DEVICES]`.
2. `static cuda_stream_expert_cache g_stream_expert_cache;` -> `[DS4_CUDA_MAX_DEVICES]` (note: contains std::vector<slot>; array-of-struct is fine, default-constructed per element).
3. g_stream_expert_budget_override / _runtime_cap / _memory_cap_notice / _runtime_gate_bytes / _runtime_down_bytes (196-200): budget_override is a USER SETTING (set once via CLI for all GPUs) — KEEP SCALAR, but the runtime_cap/runtime_gate_bytes/runtime_down_bytes/memory_cap_notice are PER-DEVICE OOM/sizing state -> make those four `[DS4_CUDA_MAX_DEVICES]`. (Each 16GB GPU may shrink its cap independently after OOM.)
4. Staging pool g_stream_selected_stage_raw/_stage/_stage_event/_stage_bytes/_upload_stream (218-222): pinned host staging + a CUDA stream are bound to the active device's context -> make all five `[DS4_CUDA_MAX_DEVICES]`. (Matches how g_pp_stream/g_tp_stream are per-device in fork: 105,608.)
5. g_ssd_streaming_mode (94): this is a global ON/OFF mode flag, identical across GPUs -> KEEP SCALAR. Do NOT array-ify (it gates behavior, not resources).

MECHANICAL RULE for the helper band (1411-2150): every bare reference `g_stream_expert_cache.X` / `g_stream_selected_cache.X` / the five staging globals / the four runtime globals becomes `[dev]`-indexed where `dev` is a new parameter threaded through, OR computed at the top of each helper via `int dev=0; cudaGetDevice(&dev); if(dev<0||dev>=DS4_CUDA_MAX_DEVICES) dev=0;`. Recommended: thread an explicit `int dev` parameter into the leaf helpers (_prepare, _find, _lru_slot, _copy_to_compact, _load_slot, _seed_one, release_all, invalidate, _try_alloc on the staging side, ensure_bytes/_i32, stage_pool_alloc, copy_to_device_streamed) and pass compact_dev from the call site, rather than calling cudaGetDevice inside hot leaf functions (avoids per-expert driver query in the decode loop). The selected-cache validity probe (upstream 12262-12289 region, which in the fork is the new streaming branch) must compare against g_stream_selected_cache[compact_dev].

TEARDOWN: the fork already loops `for(int cd=0; cd<DS4_CUDA_MAX_DEVICES; cd++)` freeing g_moe_compact_* (FORK 2784-2790). Add the per-device cuda_stream_selected_cache_release(cd)/cuda_stream_expert_cache_release_all(cd)/cuda_stream_selected_stage_release(cd) into that same loop. ds4_gpu_set_ssd_streaming and the budget setters (upstream 2757-2777) must iterate all devices (cudaSetDevice(cd) before freeing, since cudaFree is context-bound) when tearing caches down — upstream's single-shot release is a multi-GPU correctness bug for us.

SEED/BUDGET: ds4.c wiring (SPEC step 5) that calls seed_experts / set_streaming_expert_cache_budget must loop devices (cudaSetDevice each) so every PP stage gets its hotlist-seeded resident cache. Upstream never ran multi-GPU streaming, so this loop does not exist upstream.
patches.graph_capture_handling:
SPEC risk #2 — the streaming begin_compact_load does a host-side D2H read of selected ids + host LRU bookkeeping + sync, which is ILLEGAL inside an active CUDA graph capture. The fork already has the exact guard pattern to reuse: in routed_moe_launch the compact block detects capture via `int capture_active=0; if(g_cuda_decode_stream_created){cudaStreamCaptureStatus st; if(cudaSuccess==cudaStreamIsCapturing(ds4_decode_stream(),&st)) capture_active=(st==cudaStreamCaptureStatusActive);}` (FORK 12680-12685) and takes a capture-safe fast path at 12686-12690 (uses the pre-seeded g_moe_compact_* buffers, no host read).

For the streaming port, the new streaming branch (inserted before the existing else at FORK 12691) MUST be gated `if(!capture_active)`. When capture IS active, fall through to the existing capture-safe compact buffers (12686-12690) — i.e. streaming pre-seeds the resident cache + compact buffer OUTSIDE capture (via ds4_gpu_stream_expert_cache_prepare_selected_batch / seed at decode-prep time), then capture replays the kernels against already-populated g_stream_selected_cache[dev].{gate,up,down}_ptr. Also note the fork already advertises this constraint: ds4_gpu_decode_graph_can_capture (FORK 443-456) prints \"graph capture disabled: MoE weights are streamed\" — so the simplest correct integration is to let streamed layers DISABLE decode-graph capture (return 0 from can_capture when g_ssd_streaming_mode), which sidesteps the host-read-in-capture hazard entirely at the cost of per-kernel launch overhead on streamed layers. Recommend wiring g_ssd_streaming_mode into ds4_gpu_decode_graph_can_capture as the conservative first cut; optimize to pre-seed-then-capture later.

risks: Per-device array-ify is the load-bearing change: g_stream_expert_cache/g_stream_selected_cache + the 5 staging globals + 4 runtime-sizing globals MUST become [DS4_CUDA_MAX_DEVICES] indexed by compact_dev (cudaGetDevice). Leaving any single-device causes PP-stage thrash/corruption (SPEC risk #1). g_ssd_streaming_mode and budget_override stay scalar.

g_stream_expert_cache contains a std::vector<cuda_stream_expert_cache_slot>; an array-of-16 default-constructs 16 vectors — fine, but cuda_stream_expert_cache_release_all/_invalidate must operate on [dev] not a global, and the memset(&cache,0,...) trick upstream uses (1428,1442) would CLOBBER the vector for the device entry — replace memset with explicit field reset for the expert_cache struct (selected_cache memset is OK, no vector).

cudaFree/cudaFreeHost/cudaStreamDestroy are context-bound: teardown and ds4_gpu_set_ssd_streaming(false) must cudaSetDevice(cd) before freeing each device's caches. Upstream's single-shot release (2764-2766) is a multi-GPU leak/UB for us.

CUDA-graph capture hazard (SPEC risk #2): begin_compact_load does host D2H + LRU bookkeeping illegal under active capture. Gate the new streaming branch in routed_moe_launch with the existing capture_active probe (FORK 12680-12685) and/or make ds4_gpu_decode_graph_can_capture (FORK 443) return 0 when g_ssd_streaming_mode.

METAL-SAFETY: every NEW extern "C" ds4_gpu_* listed above is reachable from shared ds4.c. Each needs a Metal stub in ds4_metal.m OR an #ifndef __APPLE__ guard at the ds4.c call site, else the Metal build breaks silently (CUDA build never compiles ds4_metal.o).

O_DIRECT vs page-cache (SPEC risk #3): cuda_model_copy_to_device_streamed reads via cuda_model_stage_read which prefers g_model_direct_fd (O_DIRECT, bypasses page cache). For the 1024GB-resident strategy DS4_CUDA_NO_DIRECT_IO=1 + DS4_CUDA_KEEP_MODEL_PAGES=1 MUST be set together; ds4_gpu_set_model_fd (FORK 3101) already honors NO_DIRECT_IO. Verify the streamed-copy path actually falls back to g_model_fd (buffered) when direct fd is closed.

g_ssd_streaming_mode is currently declared-but-unread in the fork (only the declaration at 94 exists). Porting the engine introduces the first readers; confirm no name clash and that ds4.c never expected it to mean something else.

The staging-pool/ensure helpers (upstream 1692-1818) are NOT the fork's g_model_stage pool — they are a separate selected-stream pool. Do not accidentally alias them onto the fork's existing g_model_stage[4]; port them as distinct per-device globals.

Per-expert cudaGetDevice() inside leaf helpers (_load_slot/_seed_one) called in the decode hot loop would add driver-query latency; thread an explicit int dev parameter from routed_moe_launch's compact_dev (FORK 12627) instead of querying per call.

patches.per_device_adaptation: This public-api component itself defines no per-device buffers, but its function BODIES read/write the single-device streaming globals (g_ssd_streaming_mode, g_stream_expert_cache, g_stream_selected_cache, g_stream_expert_budget_override, g_stream_expert_runtime_cap/gate_bytes/down_bytes, g_stream_expert_memory_cap_notice) that the statics/engine components are arrayizing to [DS4_CUDA_MAX_DEVICES] to match the fork's existing g_moe_compact_*[] pattern. Therefore, after arrayization, every function in this block (set_ssd_streaming, set_streaming_expert_cache_budget, configured_count, current_count, release_resident, seed_selected, begin_selected_load, prepare_selected_batch, seed_experts, and cuda_stream_selected_cache_begin_compact_load) must resolve the current device via cudaGetDevice() and index the [dev] slot — OR ds4.c must iterate all devices when calling the once-per-process config setters (set_ssd_streaming/set_streaming_expert_cache_budget/expert_bytes), exactly as the SPEC risk #1 demands ('seed/budget も全 device 反復'). The fd globals (g_model_fd, g_model_fd_host_base, g_model_direct_fd, g_model_direct_align, g_model_file_size) are file-scoped (one GGUF) and stay single-global; do NOT arrayize them. Recommendation for the orchestrator: keep the public-api function bodies verbatim but have the launch/engine component wrap the per-device selection (either inside each body via cudaGetDevice, or by the ds4.c caller looping over GPUs); document this seam so the device-context (cudaSetDevice) is correct when these extern C functions run during PP stage execution.
risks: FORK has NO ds4_gpu_set_model_fd_for_map — the SPEC's '~2730 fork _for_map' reference is wrong. The fork's existing 1-arg ds4_gpu_set_model_fd@3085 already carries the upstream O_DIRECT body verbatim, so reconciliation = add a 2-arg _for_map and make set_model_fd delegate. Low risk, but the orchestrator must NOT expect to merge two existing _for_map bodies.

Single-device globals: every function body here touches g_ssd_streaming_mode / g_stream_*; once those become per-device arrays (other components), these bodies break unless they index by current device. This is the #1 multi-GPU correctness risk for the whole port and lands squarely on this API surface.

CUDA Graph capture incompatibility: begin_compact_load (2875-3115) does host LRU bookkeeping, H2D copies, and a host->device slot_ids memcpy — it CANNOT run during graph capture. The fork's routed_moe_launch has a capture-active fast path (~12680-12690). prepare_selected_batch/begin_selected_load must be invoked OUTSIDE capture (pre-seed compact buffers before replay) or the streamed layers must skip graph capture. This is a design seam the launch component must resolve; the public API as written assumes eager (non-captured) host orchestration.

Metal build breakage (METAL-SAFETY): 13 of these 14 APIs are called from shared ds4.c and have NO __APPLE__ guard, and the fork's ds4_metal.m has none of them (only a set_model_fd stub). Without the drafted Metal no-op stubs (or guarding every ds4.c call), the Metal link fails invisibly because CUDA builds never compile ds4_metal.o. prepare_selected_batch is the only one already header-guarded for __APPLE__.

Return-value semantics must be preserved on Metal stubs: configured_count==0 signals 'streaming unconfigured' to ds4.c gating (`< DS4_N_EXPERT`), and seed/begin/prepare return 1 (success-noop) matching the CUDA `if(!g_ssd_streaming_mode)return 1;` convention. A stub returning 0 from seed/begin would make ds4.c treat streaming setup as a hard failure on Metal.

cuda_stream_selected_cache_begin_compact_load is `static` (file-local) in upstream and depends on a large set of static helpers (cuda_stream_expert_cache_prepare/find/lru_slot/load_slot/copy_to_compact, cuda_stream_selected_ensure_bytes/i32, cuda_stream_layer_expert_ranges_valid, cuda_model_copy_to_device_streamed, cuda_model_load_progress_finish). Those live in the statics/helpers component (upstream ~132-2240). This public-api block will not compile in isolation — it must be grafted AFTER that helper component, or the orchestrator gets undefined-reference errors.

ds4_gpu_set_streaming_expert_cache_budget(uint32_t) — ds4_gpu.h:75; called per-device in ds4.c warm loop. Needs Metal stub (no-op) or #ifndef __APPLE__ guard.

patches.graph_capture_handling: PREFERRED (ship first): disable CUDA graph capture for MoE-bearing layers whenever g_ssd_streaming_mode!=0. Gate the subgraph capture (ds4_gpu_decode_subgraph_capture ~FORK 263) and pp_chunk_graph_capture_begin (FORK 304) so streamed layers are NOT captured; the streaming gather then runs eagerly on the decode stream each step (host D2H of selected ids + LRU bookkeeping + RAM/SSD->HBM copies + slot_ids upload — all illegal inside capture). Rationale: in streaming mode decode is dominated by the expert copy latency, so the launch-overhead savings a captured graph provides are negligible, and eager execution is the only way the host-side LRU fill is guaranteed to run before the kernels read the buffer. ADVANCED (future): keep the graph by pre-seeding — run prepare_selected_batch for every streamed layer on a non-captured stream to fill per-(dev,layer) selected caches, then replay; requires g_stream_selected_cache[dev][layer] (big VRAM) so layer L's buffer survives until its replay. Pointer stability for any captured streamed layer must be ensured by sizing cuda_stream_selected_ensure_bytes to the worst case (n_tokens*n_expert*expert_bytes, not the dedup compact_count) on the prime pass so no post-capture cudaMalloc realloc invalidates the baked pointer. FAILURE MODES: gather-during-capture -> cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported (capture aborts / PP may hang); capture-without-host-refill-on-replay -> NO crash but reads previous step's experts -> silent logit/quality collapse that masquerades as a quant bug.
patches.per_device_adaptation: Index every grafted streaming global by compact_dev (already computed at FORK 12627-12629). Convert upstream singles to arrays: g_stream_selected_cache[DS4_CUDA_MAX_DEVICES], g_stream_expert_cache[DS4_CUDA_MAX_DEVICES], and the runtime caps g_stream_expert_runtime_cap/_runtime_gate_bytes/_runtime_down_bytes/_memory_cap_notice[DS4_CUDA_MAX_DEVICES]. Keep g_ssd_streaming_mode and g_stream_expert_budget_override scalar (policy). In each grafted helper (cuda_stream_selected_cache_invalidate, cuda_stream_expert_cache_prepare/_find/_lru_slot/_load_slot/_copy_to_compact, cuda_stream_selected_cache_begin_compact_load, and the public prepare_selected_batch/seed_selected/seed_experts) add at top: int dev=0; cudaGetDevice(&dev); if(dev<0||dev>=DS4_CUDA_MAX_DEVICES)dev=0; then index [dev] on all g_stream_* accesses. In ds4.c the budget-set and hotlist-seed config MUST loop over all devices (cudaSetDevice(d) per iteration) or only GPU0 is warmed. Failure if not done per-device: cudaErrorIllegalAddress on non-GPU0 layers, or silent cross-device wrong-weight reads (garbage logits that look perfect on GPU0's layers).

risks: SEAM 3 (layer id) is a hard blocker I discovered: ds4_gpu_routed_moe_one_tensor (decode, FORK 13311) passes no layer index and routed_moe_launch has no layer param, yet the GPU-LRU keys cache slots by (model_map,layer,expert). Without a real layer id every layer collides under layer=0 -> false LRU hits return another layer's expert weights -> silent garbage. MUST thread a layer id (prefer explicit param on both extern entries + routed_moe_launch; the batch entry already receives layer_index but discards it at 13321). Until fixed, the streaming path is unusable.

Dedup vs per-pair layout mismatch is safe ONLY because I redirect selected_ptr to slot_selected_ptr in lockstep with the three weight bases. If a future edit sets gate_w/up_w/down_w from the stream cache but leaves selected_ptr on g_moe_compact_selected_dev (or selected->ptr), the kernels index dedup-packed weights with per-pair/raw indices -> out-of-bounds reads / wrong experts. The three-way selected_ptr ternary must stay coupled to use_stream.

Graph capture: if SEAM 2 (a) is not applied and a streamed MoE layer gets captured, the host LRU fill is skipped on replay -> reads prior step's experts -> quality collapse with no crash (worst debugging case). Ship with capture disabled for streamed layers first.

O_DIRECT vs page-cache (SPEC risk 3): cuda_model_copy_to_device_streamed's default DONTNEED + O_DIRECT bypasses the 1024GB page cache the whole streaming strategy depends on. DS4_CUDA_KEEP_MODEL_PAGES=1 + DS4_CUDA_NO_DIRECT_IO=1 must be set together or every miss hits Optane. Not a code bug but a config landmine that makes streaming look broken (slow).

Per-device VRAM: 7 copies of g_stream_expert_cache slots[] (the LRU) + per-device selected caches. The budget (DS4_CUDA_STREAMING_EXPERT_CACHE_N / RESERVE_GB) is per-GPU; on 16GB cards with KV+scratch reserved, an over-large budget OOMs on devices that also hold resident non-MoE weights. Verbose hit/miss logging per device is needed to tune.

cuda_model_copy_to_device_streamed rides our fork's cuda_model_stage_read/fd plumbing (SPEC risk 5) which may have diverged from upstream's quad-buffer event model (UP 214-222 g_model_stage*). Diff before grafting; if the staging event model differs, the streamed copy can race (read stale staging buffer) -> intermittent wrong weights.

Metal: the config setters (set_ssd_streaming, set_streaming_expert_cache_budget, seed_experts, etc.) are called from shared ds4.c and are NOT Apple-guarded in the header -> without the Metal stubs above, ds4_metal.o fails to link and the Mac build breaks invisibly (CUDA build never compiles ds4_metal.o, so CI on this box won't catch it).

patches.summary:
Mapped the fork's diverged option/engine/CLI/Metal layout against upstream e34a808 and produced surgical edits for engine-wiring + the 6 Metal no-op stubs.

KEY DIVERGENCE FINDINGS (load-bearing):
1. The fork's `ds4_engine_options` (ds4.h:63-77) is the SMALL legacy version — it lacks ALL six ssd_streaming*/simulate fields. Upstream's full struct (ds4.h:94-121) also has expert_profile_path/load_slice/prefill_chunk/distributed; we add ONLY the six the SPEC names.
2. The fork's ds4.c has ZERO ssd_streaming references and NO `ds4_backend_supports_ssd_streaming` — must be added.
3. CRITICAL BLOCKER for the span path: upstream's `--ssd-streaming` span-restricted `ds4_gpu_set_model_map_spans` block (upstream ds4.c:25775-25839) depends on `weights_model_map_token_spans`, `weights_model_map_decode_static_slice_spans`, `weights_have_output_head`, `ds4_model_map_span_vec`, `weights_streaming_non_routed_bytes`, `ds4_streaming_routed_expert_bytes`, `weights_streaming_layer_experts_uniform`, `ds4_streaming_cache_experts_for_byte_budget`, `ds4_streaming_manual_cache_safe_bytes` — grep confirms NONE exist in the fork (it has the simple 2-arg `weights_bind` at ds4.c:3177, not the 7-arg slice version). So the span path and byte-budget→experts conversion CANNOT be grafted in this component; they belong to a 'weights-streaming' component. My engine wiring is therefore the MINIMAL-SAFE version: copy opt->e fields, call `ds4_gpu_set_ssd_streaming(e->ssd_streaming)` + `ds4_gpu_set_streaming_expert_cache_budget(e->ssd_streaming_cache_experts)` (count-only; byte budget left for the weights component), keep the existing full `ds4_gpu_set_model_map_range` path unchanged. The span restriction (DS4_CUDA_KEEP_MODEL_PAGES makes full map acceptable initially anyway) is flagged as a follow-up.
4. The auto-cache (`ds4_engine_configure_streaming_auto_cache`) is a no-op for our CUDA build: upstream `ds4_backend_supports_streaming_auto_cache` returns false for CUDA on non-ROCm builds. Safe to omit; CLI count/GB is the path.
5. `ds4_ssd.c`/`ds4_ssd.h` are self-contained plain C (only need ds4_ssd.h); they hold the CLI parse helpers `ds4_parse_gib_arg`/`ds4_parse_streaming_cache_experts_arg` AND `ds4_ssd_memory_lock_*`. Upstream brings ds4_ssd.h in via ds4.h (upstream ds4.h:9). I replicate that so ds4.c + ds4_cli.c get the helpers transitively.
6. BUILD RISK: the fork Makefile CORE_OBJS = `ds4.o ds4_cuda.o` (and `ds4.o ds4_metal.o` on Darwin) has NO `ds4_ssd.o`. Since CLI now calls ds4_parse_* and engine close calls ds4_ssd_memory_lock_release, `ds4_ssd.o` MUST be added to CORE_OBJS on BOTH branches (CUDA, Metal) and the CPU branch too (ds4_cli is shared) or the link fails with undefined refs.
7. HOTLIST PLACEMENT CORRECTION: SPEC step (e) says include `ds4_streaming_hotlist.inc` in ds4.c, but the fork's ds4.c has NO `metal_graph_streaming_expert_hotlist_*` consumers (upstream's only consumers). Including it in ds4.c yields unused file-scope `static const` arrays → clang's -Wunused-const-variable (in -Wall) would warn (fork CFLAGS = -Wall -Wextra, no -Werror, so non-fatal, but noisy). The real consumer is the CUDA seed path in ds4_cuda.cu (DS4_CUDA_ENABLE_STREAMING_EXPERT_HOTLIST). RECOMMEND: the CUDA component `#include`s the .inc in ds4_cuda.cu, NOT ds4.c. I did NOT add it to ds4.c.

METAL STUBS: fork ds4_metal.m already has real `ds4_gpu_set_model_map_range` (4867) + no-op `ds4_gpu_set_model_fd` (4912). It is MISSING stubs for the 6 streaming APIs and has NONE of the streaming globals (g_ssd_streaming_mode, g_stream_expert_cache). Per the METAL-SAFETY RULE all 6 get disabled/no-op stubs (Metal=single-device, no streaming) inserted right after ds4_gpu_set_model_fd. `set_model_map_spans` delegates to the existing range mapper so the Metal build still maps the model.
